title: Service Sentry: per-tenant/model adaptive trip thresholds and deterministic safe fallbacks
creator: Samira Cho
description: Goal: Implement a runtime 'Service Sentry' layer that maintains adaptive per-entity (tenant/model/dependency) trip thresholds and provides deterministic and safe fallback behaviors for host-level and regional failures. This ticket covers algorithm design, runtime integration, rollout plan, and observability requirements. The intent is to reduce customer-visible errors during transient overloads or degraded downstreams while maintaining SLOs and predictable cost behavior.
background_and_rationale: Current circuit breaker approaches are global or per-service with static thresholds which either trip too aggressively for low-volume tenants or too slowly for noisy tenants. We need an adaptive, composable mechanism that accounts for entity volume, multi-region health, and model-tail latency distributions. It should be deterministic (so rollbacks and debugging are straightforward) and produce a safe fallback when a primary model or region is unhealthy.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime component (Service Sentry) deployed behind feature flag in acceptance environment
Per-tenant and per-model EWMA-based health score computed and exported as metrics
Adaptive trip threshold algorithm documented and implemented: uses percentiles, EWMA, and traffic-weighted smoothing
Safe fallback selection implemented: deterministic fallback routing to compatible model variant or remote region according to policy table
Fallbacks executed without token double-billing and with consistent error codes for tracing
End-to-end load-test demonstrating <1% user-visible error amplification under simulated N+1 region outage and 20% degraded latency on primary region
Dashboard panels and alerts for health score, trip rate, fallout rate, and fallback success rate present in Console
Runbook updated and on-call engineers trained for Sentry behaviors
implementation_notes: Design a health score per entity: combine 95th latency percentile, error-rate, and request success ratio into 0..100 score using EWMA windows (1m, 5m, 1h)

Adaptive threshold formula: trip if health_score < dynamic_threshold(entity_volume) for >= min_duration, where dynamic_threshold reduces for high-volume entities and raises for low-volume ones to avoid noisy trips
Volume weighting: threshold = base_threshold + alpha / sqrt(requests_per_minute + epsilon) to scale sensitivity
Deterministic fallback selection: use config table ordered by preference and a stable hash of request_id to evenly distribute fallbacks when multiple candidates are available
Fallback safety: tag fallback requests with provenance headers, ensure downstream metering does not double-bill tokens, and persist original request metadata for tracing
Integration points: Service Sentry sits between router and model runner; it subscribes to per-node health signals and to cross-region heartbeat channel
Circuit state machine: CLOSED -> MONITORING -> OPEN -> HYSTERESIS -> RECOVERING -> CLOSED with explicit transitions and timeouts
Expose debug endpoint gated by admin flag to fetch current entity policy and state for debugging (read-only)
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Unit tests + simulation harness validating thresholds against synthetic traffic distributions
Phase 1: Canary in staging behind feature flag for 5 internal tenants, monitor metrics for 48h
Phase 2: Progressive rollout to 10% of production traffic with automatic rollback if fallout_rate > 0.5% or user_error_rate increases
Phase 3: Region-aware canary: introduce controlled latency in primary region to validate multi-region failover behavior
Phase 4: Full rollout with runbook enablement and postrollout review
testing_plan: Unit tests for health score aggregation and threshold math
Integration test harness that replays production latency/error traces and verifies deterministic fallbacks
Chaos test: kill model runner in primary region while asserting fallback routing to secondary region and no silent failures
Load test: spike traffic for low-volume tenant to ensure thresholds do not cause noisy-open; expect stable degrading to fallback rather than oscillation
Billing test: validate token accounting for fallback requests across runners and regions
open_questions: What is the canonical list of fallback-compatible model variants for each primary model? (PD required)
Do we need a per-tenant opt-out for automatic fallback for compliance or audit reasons?
What SLO breach budget should we consume before allowing regional failover to count as successful?
Should fallback requests be rate-limited differently to protect secondary capacity?
Is there an ops-approved default dynamic_threshold curve or should it be tunable per-tenant?
security_considerations: Service Sentry will surface per-tenant state and debugging endpoints; ensure RBAC gating and auditing on reads. Fallback provenance headers must not leak internal topology or secrets. KMS-protected configs where applicable.

notes_for_oncall: If Service Sentry trips for many tenants simultaneously, follow runbook: 1) Check sentry.entity.health_score dashboards, 2) Inspect region heartbeat, 3) If widespread false positives, temporarily disable sentry by feature flag and open incident, 4) Coordinate rollback and communicate to affected customers.
